failures.name: First layer failed
failures.player_text: The first layer looks like a plate of noodles. Nothing else is going to stick to that.

failures.name: Print came loose
failures.player_text: The print let go halfway and is now being pushed around like a hockey puck.

failures.name: Spaghetti monster
failures.player_text: The printer has spent hours knitting a bird's nest. Silently. Lovingly.

failures.name: Nozzle clog
failures.fix: Clear the nozzle with a cold pull
failures.player_text: The printer is very confidently printing nothing at all.

failures.name: Tangled spool
failures.player_text: A knot formed somewhere deep in the spool. Nobody knows how. Nobody ever knows how.

failures.name: Corners warped
failures.player_text: The corners have curled up. It still sort of works, if your customer doesn't own a ruler.

failures.name: Layer shift
failures.fix: Tall prints on a bed slinger are the risky ones
failures.player_text: Halfway up, the whole print decided to move one centimetre to the left. Bold choice.

failures.name: Under extrusion
failures.fix: Usually a sign the hotend wants attention
failures.player_text: Looks like it was printed by someone who was rationing plastic.

failures.name: Stringy mess
failures.fix: Some filaments string more than others
failures.player_text: It's covered in fine little hairs. Seasonal for Halloween. Less so for a phone stand.

failures.name: Rough surface finish
failures.fix: A finer preset gives a smoother finish
failures.player_text: It works, but it has the texture of a cheese grater.
